newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - April in Asia.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - April in Asia.

text.p: Asian debt markets were quiet on Friday, but details emerged on a deal for Indonesia's April.
Bear Stearns Asia announced terms on a US$50 million transaction for Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings (APRIL), an Indonesian pulp and paper company.
The notes have a final maturity of three years and annual put and call options. The coupon range is indicated at 225 to 237.5 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the notes pay a simple yield to the put of LIBOR plus 275 to 287.5 basis points.
PT April's main assets are a 98.9 percent ownership interest in PT Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper (RAPP) and an effective 61.3 percent ownership interest in PT Inti Indorayon Utama.

As part of its strategy to become an integrated pulp and paper producer, APRIL is in the process of diversifying from its core pulp business into downstream paper and paperboard manufacturing, Bear Stearns noted.

To this end, it has entered into a joint venture with South Korea's Hansol Paper to construct a mill in Indonesia to produce uncoated free-sheet paper, the type of paper commonly used by photocopiers and computer printers.
The PT April issue is part of a US$300 million guaranteed Asian Currency Note Programme. Bear Stearns also has established a US$300 million guaranteed ACN for a unit of Lippo Land.
More details emerged on Thursday's one billion Deutschemark Euro-Asian bond for Germany's Depfa.
It appears that about half of the deal placed in Asia.
"Of our total allotment, about 55 percent placed into Asia, about evenly between Japan and non-Japan Asia," said a syndicate manager involved in the transaction.
The share of paper that went to Asia was placed among a few large institutional investors. Though the number of investors was small, they were fairly evenly distributed in the region.
"There wasn't a long list of buyers. They were accounts that are comfortable holding Dmarks and are capable of holding size," said the syndicate manager.
Depfa has issued Pfandbrief globals, but this is its first deal that was sold to Europe and Asia but not the U.S. The bond is the first Euro-Asian Pfandbrief.
Pfandbrief bonds are mortgage bonds issued by mortgage banks in Germany and secured by their mortgage lendings.
Traders said confusion concerning the U.S. response to Malaysian state oil company Petronas's involvement in projects with Iran appears to have had little impact on the company's recent bond issue.

"We did see some jump in the five-year tranche, but then it settled down," said one trader. "But it is hard to detect because of the massive rally in U.S. Treasuries that has caused some slippage in spreads generally," he said.
On Tuesday, an aide to U.S. senator Alfonse D'Amato said the the senate sanctions committe had recommended action against Petronas because of its involvement with Iranian interests.
New York senator D'Amato is the architect of a controversial law requiring sanctions on U.S. companies that invest in oil and gas projects in Iran and Libya.
But the U.S. embassy in Malaysia said Friday that the U.S. has not taken or recommended any action against Petronas.
